messages.subject: About lp__
parts:
Just to be sure :

I understand that a sampling statement such as "Y~foo(a,b)" increments lp__ by foo_log(a,b) minus constant terms, whereas "increment_log_prob(foo_log(Y,a,b)"  increments lp__ by foo_log(a,b) exactly.

In other word, lp__ is the log-posterior if and only if  there is no sampling statements in the model.

Is this right ?

Bonus question (rstan) : does "get_logposterior(modelfit)" does anything different of "extract(modelfit, "lp__")[[1]]"?

--
Emmanuel Charpentier

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] About lp__
parts:
> On Apr 12, 2015, at 5:13 PM, Emmanuel Charpentier <emanuel.c...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Just to be sure :
>
> I understand that a sampling statement such as "Y~foo(a,b)" increments lp__ by foo_log(a,b) minus constant terms,

The constant terms are terms that only involve double values.
So it depends what the arguments are as to what's constant.
> whereas "increment_log_prob(foo_log(Y,a,b)" increments lp__ by foo_log(a,b) exactly.

> In other word, lp__ is the log-posterior if and only if there is no sampling statements in the model.
>
> Is this right ?

Almost. There's also the Jacobians of the inverse transforms for
the constraints. If you declare a variable

real<lower=0> x;

then there's a log transform of x in (0,inf) to y = log(x) in (-inf,inf).
That means there's an exp inverse transform back from y in (-inf,inf) to
x = exp(y) in (0,inf). To adjust for the change of variables,

log abs( d/dy exp(y)) = y = log(x)

gets added to lp__.
> Bonus question (rstan) : does "get_logposterior(modelfit)" does anything different of "extract(modelfit, "lp__")[[1]]"?

No idea about that one --- it's an RStan issue.

- Bob
